name: Michigan veterans: benefits and accredited claims referrals
description: MVAA connects veterans and families to benefits counselors and community support.
next_step: Give your county and ask for an accredited representative, benefits review and help obtaining discharge documents.

name: MI Options: care and disability counseling
organization: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
description: Statewide counseling helps adults explore long-term care, community supports and aging at home.
next_step: Call for a local counselor; describe the daily-living need and ask for a practical referral plan.

name: Michigan aging services: local assessment
organization: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
description: Regional aging agencies coordinate meals, caregiving, transportation and home support.
next_step: Choose your county for its agency contacts. In Wayne County, use the agency serving the resident’s city.
constraints: Local assessment, program eligibility, cost sharing and availability vary.

name: MI Choice Medicaid waiver
organization: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
description: Approved home and community services can include care, respite, equipment and environmental accessibility adaptations.
next_step: Use the official waiver-agency list to request screening. Enrolled participants should contact their supports coordinator before arranging work.
constraints: Income, assets, nursing-facility level of care and other program criteria apply. Assessment and service-plan authorization are required; a referral does not guarantee enrollment.

name: Home Help: personal assistance at home
organization: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
description: Medicaid-supported assistance with approved daily activities following an Adult Services assessment.
next_step: Contact the Adult Services unit at your county MDHHS office for a Home Help referral and medical-needs paperwork.
constraints: Medicaid Fee for Service eligibility and physical help with at least one activity of daily living are required. Home Help excludes home repairs, supervision and transportation.

name: Michigan SHIP: free Medicare counseling
organization: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
description: Unbiased counselors explain Medicare coverage, enrollment and potential savings programs.
next_step: Call MI Options and ask for a local certified Medicare counselor.

name: Michigan long-term-care ombudsman
organization: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
description: Resident advocacy addresses care and quality-of-life concerns in licensed long-term-care facilities.
next_step: Give the facility county and ask to connect with the local ombudsman. For immediate danger, call 911.

name: Michigan Assistive Technology Program: trials and loans
description: Free demonstrations and temporary device loans help people explore assistive technology.
next_step: Describe the barrier, ask about a demonstration and check device availability and loan terms.
constraints: MATP does not provide clinical assessments. A device loan is not a permanent equipment grant or a promise of ramp installation.

name: Disability Rights Michigan
description: Protection and advocacy offers disability rights information, referrals and selected direct advocacy.
next_step: Explain the disability-related issue and ask about intake and the next step.
constraints: Direct representation depends on current priorities and capacity.

name: Blind and low-vision independent living: age 55+
organization: Michigan Bureau of Services for Blind Persons
description: Independent living instruction and adapted aids help qualifying residents with vision loss.
next_step: Ask about a services referral and the rehabilitation professional serving your county.
constraints: Age 55+ and qualifying vision loss apply. Equipment support is subject to program budgets; this is not cash assistance or transportation.

name: Michigan Relay: accessible telephone calls
organization: Michigan Public Service Commission / Hamilton Relay
description: Relay connects hearing callers and people who are Deaf, hard of hearing or have speech disabilities.
next_step: Dial 711 and ask the relay operator to help connect your call.
constraints: Relay does not supply hearing aids or establish equipment funding.

name: Creating Confident Caregivers
organization: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
description: Classes support family caregivers of people living with dementia at home.
next_step: Use the state page to find a participating partner and ask about upcoming classes and registration.
constraints: Eligibility and space limits apply. Participating class partners do not represent the full aging-agency coverage map.

name: Michigan veteran emergency assistance
description: MVAA routes temporary financial needs to possible emergency resources, including county relief and the Veterans Trust Fund.
next_step: Describe the expense and urgency. Ask the county committee or MVAA about a complete application and required documents.
constraints: Trust Fund eligibility includes Michigan residence, discharge and qualifying service requirements. A resource-assistance form is not a Trust Fund application; funds and approval are not guaranteed.

name: Michigan PACE: coordinated community care
organization: Michigan Department of Health and Human Services
description: Participating PACE organizations coordinate medical and social support for eligible adults.
next_step: Check the official provider list for coverage of your ZIP code, then ask that provider for an assessment.
constraints: Age 55+, nursing-facility level of care, an approved service area and safe community living at enrollment are required. PACE and MI Choice cannot be enrolled concurrently.
